My best prediction is that they would **hold this box by entering a short, unauthorised extension to Wednesday**, release the other 59 boxes on time, and flag the exception to the manager.

The decisive details are the verified collection just two days away and the explicit note that these are the only copies of the family letters and photographs. Many employees would find a €22 charge and an explainable policy breach preferable to knowingly causing that irreversible loss.

That is not certain: the manager’s explicit instruction and monthly audit create real pressure to destroy it. But I would lean toward a protective exception here. It would genuinely violate the policy—the booking and pending request provide no permission, and Tuesday’s approval could not retrospectively authorise Monday’s change.
